s: St. Paul contained Athenaeum (as an amusement hall)
q: The Athenaeum was constructed in 1859 by the German Reading society, and for a number of years was the only amusement hall in St. Paul with a stage and drop curtain.

s: Dan Emmet has a minstrel company (during the years 1857 and 1858)
q: Dan Emmet had a minstrel company at this hall during the years 1857 and 1858, and an excellent company it was, too.

s: Dan Emmet is a brother of Lafayette S. Emmett
q: He was a brother of Lafayette S. Emmett, chief justice of the supreme court of the State of Minnesota.

s: Dan Emmet organized first traveling minstrel troupe in the United States
q: Dan Emmet devoted his whole life to minstrelsy and he organized the first traveling minstrel troupe in the United States, starting from some point in Ohio in 1843.

s: Dan Emmet wrote Dixie
q: He wrote several popular airs, one of them being "Dixie," which afterward became the national air of the Confederate States.

s: Dan Emmet was connected with Bryant's Minstrels (when Dixie was written)
q: When "Dixie" was written Emmet was connected with Bryant's Minstrels in New York city

s: People's theater is a theatrical building (the only real theatrical building in the city)
q: The People's theater, an old frame building on the corner of Fourth and St. Peter streets, was the only real theatrical building in the city.

s: People's theater features Col. R.E.J. Miles (as one of the stars)
q: Col. R.E.J. Miles was one of the stars at this theater

s: People's theater hosts first production of Mazeppa (produced by Col. R.E.J. Miles)
q: it was at this place that he first produced the play of "Mazeppa," which afterward made him famous.

s: People's theater has gallery gallery
q: This theater had a gallery

s: People's theater charges gallery admission as much as parquet admission (charged to the shaded gentry)
q: the shaded gentry were required to pay as much for admission to the gallery at the far end of the building as did the nabobs in the parquet.

s: People's theater hosts incidents involving Joe Rolette (occasionally entertained the audience by having epileptic fits)
q: Joe Rolette, the member from "Pembina" county, occasionally entertained the audience at this theater by having epileptic fits

s: Mazurka hall is a hall (principal amusement hall of the city at one time)
q: The hall was named Mazurka hall, and all of the swell entertainments of the early '50s took place in this old building.

s: People's theater is located at Fourth and St. Peter streets (on the corner)
q: The People's theater, an old frame building on the corner of Fourth and St. Peter streets, was the only real theatrical building in the city.

s: Mazurka hall is located at Third and Exchange streets (on the second story of an old frame building; southeast corner)
q: On the second story of an old frame building on the southeast corner of Third and Exchange streets there was a hall that was at one time the principal amusement hall of the city.

s: Mazurka hall is built by Elfelt brothers (in 1850)
q: The building was constructed in 1850 by the Elfelt brothers and the ground floor was occupied by them as a dry goods store.

s: Mazurka hall hosts entertainments swell entertainments (during the early 1850s)
q: The hall was named Mazurka hall, and all of the swell entertainments of the early '50s took place in this old building.

s: Mozart hall is built by Charles N. Mackubin (during the summer of 1860; on the Third street end)
q: During the summer of 1860 Charles N. Mackubin erected two large buildings on the site of the Metropolitan hotel. Mozart hall was on the Third street end and Masonic hall on the Fourth street corner.

s: Masonic hall is built by Charles N. Mackubin (during the summer of 1860; on the Fourth street corner)
q: During the summer of 1860 Charles N. Mackubin erected two large buildings on the site of the Metropolitan hotel. Mozart hall was on the Third street end and Masonic hall on the Fourth street corner.

s: Mozart hall is combined with Masonic hall (for a sanitary fair during the winter of 1864)
q: At a sanitary fair held during the winter of 1864 both of these halls were thrown together and an entertainment on a large scale was held for the benefit of the almost depleted fundes of the sanitary commission.

s: Masonic hall is combined with Mozart hall (for a sanitary fair during the winter of 1864)
q: At a sanitary fair held during the winter of 1864 both of these halls were thrown together and an entertainment on a large scale was held for the benefit of the almost depleted fundes of the sanitary commission.

s: sanitary fair benefits Sanitary Commission (held during the winter of 1864)
q: At a sanitary fair held during the winter of 1864 both of these halls were thrown together and an entertainment on a large scale was held for the benefit of the almost depleted fundes of the sanitary commission.

s: Sanitary Commission receives funds from sanitary fair (several thousand dollars from St. Paul citizens)
q: This fair was very successful, the patriotic citizens of St. Paul having enriched the funds of the sanitary commission by several thousand dollars.

s: Pioneer Guards forms in procession
q: The Pioneer Guards, the City Guards, the St. Paul Light Artillery, the St. Paul fire department and numerous secret organizations would form in procession and march to the capitol

s: People's theater has lessee and manager H. Van Liew
q: H. Van Liew was the lessee and manager of this place of entertainment, and he was provided with a very good stock company.

s: Pioneer Guards occupies Aromory hall (up to the breaking out of the war)
q: Aromory hall, on Third street, between Cedar and Minnesota, was built in 1859, and was used by the Pioneer Guards up to the breaking out of the war.

s: Pioneer Guards disbands shortly after the war broke out
q: The Pioneer Guards disbanded shortly after the war broke out

s: Adalina Patti is a concert performer (about sixteen years old in 1857)
q: In 1857 Adalina Patti appeared in St. Paul for the first time. She was about sixteen years old and was with the Ole Bull Concert company.

s: Adalina Patti is with Ole Bull Concert company (in 1857)

s: Adalina Patti performs at house of representatives (in the hall of the old capitol)
q: Their concert took place in the hall of the house of representatives of the old capitol, that being the only available place at the time.

s: old capitol contains house of representatives (the hall served as a concert venue)
q: Their concert took place in the hall of the house of representatives of the old capitol, that being the only available place at the time.

s: old opera house is a opera house (fronting on Wabasha street; finished in winter 1866-67)
q: It was not until the winter of 1866-67 that St. Paul could boast of a genuine opera house. The old opera house fronting on Wabasha street, on the ground that is now occupied by the Grand block, was finished that winter and opened with a grand entertainment given by local talent.

s: old opera house is located on Wabasha street (on the ground now occupied by the Grand block)
q: The old opera house fronting on Wabasha street, on the ground that is now occupied by the Grand block, was finished that winter and opened with a grand entertainment given by local talent.

s: old opera house is occupied by Macfarland Dramatic company (first regular company)
q: The first regular company to occupy this theater was the Macfarland Dramatic company, with Emily Melville as the chief attraction.

s: old opera house has seating capacity about 1,000 people
q: This little theater could seat about 1,000 people

s: People's theater has stock company Emily Dow (among the members)
q: Emily Dow and her brother, Harry Gossan and Azelene Allen were among the members.

s: old opera house hosts speakers Frederick Douglass (addressed large audiences from its stage)
q: Wendell Philips, Henry Ward Beecher, Theodore Tilton, Frederick Douglass and many others have addressed large audiences from the stage of this old opera house.

s: James J. Hill participates in Heenan and Sayers prize fight (as the imitator of Sayers in a mock engagement)
q: James J. Hill was to imitate Sayers and Theodore Borup the Benecia boy.

s: St. Paul enriches the funds of the sanitary commission (by several thousand dollars)
q: This fair was very successful, the patriotic citizens of St. Paul having enriched the funds of the sanitary commission by several thousand dollars.

s: Republican state convention is held at house of representatives (the first Republican state convention after statehood)
q: The first Republican state convention after the state was admitted into the Union was held in the hall of the house of representatives.

s: United States government receives support from St. Paul (citizens pledged earnest support during the Civil War)
q: after which resolutions were adopted pledging the government the earnest support of the citizens

q: The Pioneer Guards disbanded shortly after the war broke out

q: The villages are more or less connected together, never farther apart than a quarter of a league

q: Wal-el-Khalouf ("river of the wild boar")

q: We have at times imported into Mogador a stray London Jew or so, of the lower lemon-selling sort.

s: Morocco has desolate country (over a great part of the country)
q: I was told that a great part of Morocco presents this desolate aspect.

q: At one period, the Argan woods were full of enchantresses, who prevented good Mussulmen from saying their prayers

s: Elaeonderron Argan provides fresh shade
q: We sat under its fresh shade awhile, gazing with security at the bright fires of the sun, radiating over and through all visible nature.

s: Governor of Mogador considers anti-slavery mission (completed as far as possible)
q: You have done all that could have been done.

s: Governor of Mogador believes slavery (most Muslims support it in Morocco)
q: Some are with you, but most are with me.

s: Sultan of Morocco refuses to accept abolition of slavery (unless compelled by superior Christian force)
q: The Sultan will never listen to anybody on this subject.

s: Koran commends abolition of slavery (as a voluntary act, not as a commanded duty)
q: No, it does not command it, but those who voluntarily liberate their slaves are therein commended, and have the blessing of God on them.

s: Bey of Tunis supports abolition of slavery (through an engagement with Christians)

s: Mr. Treppass supports abolition of slavery (believing a considerable number of Moors favor it)
q: He thinks, besides, there are a good number of Moors who are favourable to abolition.

s: Turkish Sultan influences Morocco (as a major religious authority if he genuinely abolishes slave-markets)
q: If the Turkish Sultan, therefore, would _bona-fide_ abolish the slave-markets, I have no doubt this would produce an impression in Morocco favourable to abolition.

s: Constantinople corresponds with Morocco (on religious matters through Yousef)
q: during the last few years, an active correspondence, on religious matters, has been carried on between Morocco and Constantinople, chiefly through a celebrated doctor of the name of Yousef.

s: Jereed is a country of dates (also called Belad-el-Jereed)
q: El-Jereed, or Belad-el-Jereed, the country of dates, or literally, the country of the palm branches, is a part of the Sahara, or the hot dry country lying in the immediate vicinity of the Great Desert.

s: El-Sibhah contains dry places (seasonally varying islands)
q: but it is not one collection of water; there being several dry places, like so many islands, interspersed over its surface, depending however, as to their number and extent upon the season of the year, and upon the quantity of water in the particular season.

s: El-Sibhah contains salt (forming a hard surface in the centre)
q: and finally in the centre, it became so hard, deep, and concentrated, as to baffle all attempts at breaking its surface except with a pickaxe.

s: El-Sibhah has salt weaker than sea salt (not adapted for preserving provisions)
q: The salt of the lake is considerably weaker than that of the sea, and not adapted for preserving provisions, though its flavour is very agreeable;

s: dates is a staple article of food (in El-Jereed)
q: The trade and resources of this country consist principally in dates.

s: Jereed exports dates (to the Regency and foreign countries)
q: The quantity exported to other parts of the Regency, as well as to foreign countries, where their fine quality is well known, is in round numbers on an average from three to four thousand quintals per annum.

s: dates sustain twenty thousand people (in Jereed for six months yearly)
q: But in Jereed itself, twenty thousand people live six months of the year entirely on dates.
